claims.claim: pandas 3.0.2: validate='many_to_one' raises MergeError 'Merge keys are not unique in right dataset; not a many-to-one merge'; != keeps missing values; merge matches null keys.
claims.source: Local run on pandas 3.0.2 (Pyodide pin), September 2026.

claims.claim: PySpark 4.0.4: != filter drops nulls; eqNullSafe keeps them when negated; null join keys do not match; NOT IN with a null in the subquery returns no rows; NOT EXISTS and left_anti do not.

concept_html:
Some bugs raise no error. The job succeeds and the numbers are wrong. Two of the most common come from joins and from nulls.

Join row explosion. A left join of respondents to a region lookup should keep one row per respondent. If the lookup holds a key twice, say N for "North" and "North (old)", every respondent in N appears twice. Weighted totals double for that region. Nothing fails.

Check the grain around every join:

  • Count rows before and after. A many-to-one join must not change the count.
  • In pandas, pass validate="many_to_one". A duplicate key then raises MergeError: Merge keys are not unique in right dataset. Checked on pandas 3.0.2.
  • In Spark, count duplicate keys in the lookup before joining: dim.groupBy(key).count().filter("count > 1").

Nulls behave differently in pandas and Spark. Checked on pandas 3.0.2 and PySpark 4.0.4:

Operation pandas Spark and SQL
Filter region != "N" Keeps rows where region is missing Drops rows where region is null
Join on a null key Matches null to null Never matches a null key
x NOT IN (subquery) where the subquery holds a null Not applicable Returns no rows

In Spark and SQL, a comparison with null gives null, not True or False, and a filter keeps only True. So F.col("region_code") != "N" silently drops every respondent with no region. Say what you mean:

  • Keep nulls: (F.col("region_code") != "N") | F.col("region_code").isNull(), or ~F.col("region_code").eqNullSafe("N").
  • Exclude a list that might contain nulls: use NOT EXISTS or a left_anti join, not NOT IN.

In pandas, the surprise runs the other way: null keys match each other. Drop or fill null keys before a merge unless you want that.

lines: def add_region(respondents: pd.DataFrame, regions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
"""Attach region names. One output row per respondent.
Raises:
pandas.errors.MergeError: If a region code appears twice in regions.
"""
lookup = regions.dropna(subset=["region_code"])
merged = respondents.merge(lookup, on="region_code", how="left", validate="many_to_one")
if len(merged) != len(respondents):
raise ValueError(f"join changed rows: {len(respondents)} -> {len(merged)}")
return merged

exercises.solution:
import pandas as pd


def safe_left_join(facts: pd.DataFrame, lookup: pd.DataFrame, key: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Left join that keeps the grain of facts.

    Args:
        facts: Rows to keep, one per output row.
        lookup: Attributes to attach, at most one row per key.
        key: Join column.

    Returns:
        The joined frame with len(facts) rows.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If lookup holds a key more than once, or the grain changes.
    """
    clean = lookup.dropna(subset=[key])
    counts = clean[key].value_counts()
    duplicated = sorted(counts[counts > 1].index.tolist())
    if duplicated:
        raise ValueError(f"duplicate keys in lookup: {duplicated}")
    joined = facts.merge(clean, on=key, how="left")
    if len(joined) != len(facts):
        raise ValueError(f"join changed rows: {len(facts)} -> {len(joined)}")
    return joined
solution_lines: import pandas as pd
def safe_left_join(facts: pd.DataFrame, lookup: pd.DataFrame, key: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
"""Left join that keeps the grain of facts.
Args:
facts: Rows to keep, one per output row.
lookup: Attributes to attach, at most one row per key.
key: Join column.
Returns:
The joined frame with len(facts) rows.
Raises:
ValueError: If lookup holds a key more than once, or the grain changes.
"""
clean = lookup.dropna(subset=[key])
counts = clean[key].value_counts()
duplicated = sorted(counts[counts > 1].index.tolist())
if duplicated:
raise ValueError(f"duplicate keys in lookup: {duplicated}")
joined = facts.merge(clean, on=key, how="left")
if len(joined) != len(facts):
raise ValueError(f"join changed rows: {len(facts)} -> {len(joined)}")
return joined

title: Join row explosion and nulls in filters
why_html: A regional reach table showed the North at 118% weighted reach. The region lookup had gained a second row for code N when a boundary changed. The left join doubled every northern respondent. A row count check before and after the join, or validate="many_to_one", would have stopped the job at the join.
